does: Smooths a soft paste, mash or butter over a surface in an even layer with the back of a spoon or a knife, so that every bite carries some and the edges stay clear.

intro.what: Spreading smooths a soft paste across a surface in an even layer.
intro.why: It teaches you to adjust paste consistency before applying pressure to a delicate base.

how: Have the paste soft enough to move. Loosen it with a little oil or water if it is stiff.
Put a spoonful in the middle of the surface.
Push it outwards with the back of a spoon in slow circles, working towards the edge.
Stop a little short of the edge, so that the paste does not run off or burn on the pan.

cues.text: An even layer, with the surface showing through at the thin places and a clear rim.
The spoon glides. If it drags, the paste is too stiff and wants more oil.

mistakes.mistake: Spreading a paste that is too stiff, so that it tears the dough.
mistakes.fix: Loosen it with a little oil first.

mistakes.mistake: Piling the paste in the middle and leaving the edge bare.
mistakes.fix: Push it out in circles until the layer is even, to just short of the rim.

quiz.question: Why spread filling or paste evenly?
choices: To concentrate nearly all of it in the middle.
To distribute it across bites without an overloaded centre.
To force it over the rim.
quiz.because: A consistent layer gives more even coverage while a clear rim contains it.

quiz.question: Where should spreading begin?
choices: At the rim, pushing everything off the edge.
By pressing a stiff mound repeatedly in place.
From the middle, moving outward in gentle circles.
quiz.because: Gentle outward movement distributes the paste gradually without tearing the base.

quiz.question: What should the spoon feel like as paste spreads?
choices: It catches and tears the base.
It leaves an immovable mound behind.
quiz.because: A gliding spoon indicates the paste is soft enough to distribute without excess force.

quiz.question: The paste tears the dough as you spread it. What should change?
choices: Press harder with the back of the spoon.
Loosen the stiff paste with a little oil first.
Add dry flour to thicken the paste.
quiz.because: Softening the paste addresses its resistance rather than transferring more force to the dough.
